items.title: PR feat/eval
items.body:
## Fix: corrected ablation evaluation for models v1–v4

### What was wrong
The first version of this ablation experiment evaluated all four model 
versions (v1–v4) using a single cleaning function — the same 
aggressiveness as v1's training-time cleaning — regardless of which 
model was actually being scored.

Since models v2–v4 were trained on vocabularies built from less 
aggressively cleaned data, this mismatch meant test documents were 
over-cleaned relative to what those models expected: fewer words in 
each test email matched anything in the model's vocabulary at 
prediction time. This compounded with a separate, expected effect of 
Laplace smoothing larger vocabularies inherently produce smaller 
per-word likelihoods, since the same total probability mass is spread 
across more words. Together, these two effects skewed the log-posterior 
scores for v2–v4, producing a steeper, artificial decline in precision, 
recall, F1, and accuracy than the models actually exhibit.

### Fix
- Added a separate cleaning function per model version 
  (`clean_v1`–`clean_v4`), matching each model's original training-time 
  configuration.
- `predict()` and `confusion()` now accept a `clean` function 
  parameter, so each model is evaluated using its own matching cleaning 
  logic instead of a single shared function.
- Re-ran the full evaluation with the corrected methodology. Updated 
  results, tables, and plots reflect the corrected numbers.

### Note
The original (incorrect) implementation is preserved, commented out, in 
`03_evaluate.ipynb` for reference, see the methodology note there for 
the full before/after comparison.

items.title: Cache parsed scripts instead of re-parsing them for every document
items.body:
Every document gets its own engine, and `RunScript` hands the raw source to `Engine.Evaluate(string)`, which parses it from scratch. A page that loads a library therefore pays the full parse of that library once per document, even though the result is identical every time. The same applies to any host code that calls `ExecuteScript` with the same snippet repeatedly.

### Change

Prepare the script once and evaluate the prepared form. Jint documents a prepared script as *"reusable and thread-safe"*, so one entry can serve every document that runs the same source.

Sources that fail to prepare are handed to the engine as text, so a syntax error is still reported by the engine as a `JavaScriptException` and not turned into `ScriptPreparationException`.

The cache is capped, because nothing bounds how many distinct scripts a process may see; the entries kept are the ones encountered first, which is where shared libraries show up. Happy to change the number or the policy if you would rather have something else there.

This also drops `RunScript`'s `context` parameter and the overload that fed it - the parameter was never read, and the overload that converted a node for it had no callers. Both are internal.

### Tests

Two tests added to `InteractionTests` for the properties this change must not break. They pass on `devel` too - they are guards, not regression tests:

* `RunSameScriptSourceInSeveralDocumentsKeepsStateSeparate` - the same source evaluated in two documents keeps per-document state, and stays correct across repeated evaluation;
* `RunScriptSnippetWithSyntaxErrorThrows`.

Test results are otherwise unchanged: the same six pre-existing `net8.0` failures before and after (fixed by #111; the suite is green on `net462`/`net472`).

Correct the steering text, which contradicted what #105 installed, and record the specification rule where every executor reads it. Steps 4 and 5 of #101.

## Related Issue

Closes #106. Part of #101.

## Assurance Level

- Change type: Operations
- Assurance level: Standard
- Required human approvals: Merge Authority approval on the protected `main` branch

## Standard Change

- Affected standard areas: none — no `.ai/managed/**` file is touched
- Versioning impact: None
- Downstream compatibility: unaffected; no product code
- Migration required: no

## Major Changes

### What was wrong

The Specifications section added by #103, written while the tool was still Kiro, said:

> Spec-driven work in this project writes into the standard's change packages, **not into a
> `.kiro/specs/` tree**. Per #101: a specification directory **only Kiro reads** would be an
> alternative source of truth…

After #105 merged, both halves were false:

- cc-sdd writes to `.kiro/specs/`. #101 decision 1 accepted that and made the change package the
  authoritative copy distilled from it.
- The premise — a directory only one tool reads — **lapsed**. cc-sdd ships the same skills to
  Claude Code and Codex, which is the reason it was chosen over Kiro.

What survives is the rule, not the reasoning: `.kiro/specs/` must not be the *source of truth*.
The location was never the point. Anyone running a spec on `main` today meets an instruction
contradicting the tool they were told to use.

### What changed

- `.ai/project/RULES.md` gains a **Specifications** section: where cc-sdd writes, what is
  authoritative, the change-package threshold, that tasks are Issues, that a spec does not
  authorise implementation, and **why the original prohibition lapsed**.
- `.kiro/steering/development-standard.md` drops its copy and points at `RULES.md`.
  **75 → 52 lines.**

### Why `RULES.md` and not the steering file

`AI_TOOL_COMPATIBILITY.md` treats `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.kiro/steering/**` as entry
points that "must not define conflicting standards". A rule carried only by the Kiro steering
file is the tool-specific arrangement #101 argued against — and **Codex, which now has cc-sdd
skills installed, does not read that file.** `RULES.md` is what all three point at.

Steering keeps a pointer rather than a copy. Duplication is what let these drift between #103 and
#105 in the first place, so repeating it would have reproduced the defect while fixing it.

### The lapsed premise is recorded deliberately

#101's body still contains the original "only Kiro reads it" reasoning. Someone acting on that
text alone would reinstate a prohibition whose basis has gone. `RULES.md` now states why it no
longer applies, and under what condition it would apply again — spec work returning to a
single-tool arrangement.

## Out of Scope

- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`; they already import `RULES.md`, and duplicating the rule there is
  the mistake being fixed
- The cc-sdd templates, which already carry the rule from #105
- Producing a change package on real work — #101 step 6
- `.ai/managed/**`, `lifetxt/**`, `tests/**`

## Process and Quality Viewpoints

- Lifecycle phase: Implementation -> Developer Verification -> Independent Review
- Development method: adaptive-default (continuous Kanban) with W-model gates
- Review viewpoints: Requirements review — would someone following only these documents now do the right thing? Design review — is the rule in one place with pointers rather than copies?
- Test viewpoints: none automated; see the risk below
- Coding viewpoints: documentation only
- Security viewpoints: none
- Operations viewpoints: the failure mode is an executor following a wrong instruction, which nothing reports
- Traceability: `req-ai-standard-guided-activation` -> `cap-ai-standard-guided-activation` -> #101 -> #106 -> this PR
- Capability impact: extends `cap-ai-standard-guided-activation`

## Validation Commands and Results

- [ ] Format — not applicable
- [ ] Lint — not applicable
- [ ] Unit tests — not applicable; no product code
- [ ] Integration tests — not applicable
- [ ] Standard validation — not applicable
- [ ] Standard evaluation — not applicable
- [x] Manual verification

```text
# No statement contradicting the installed layout remains in either file
grep -n "not into a|only Kiro reads|Kiro's spec"  steering, RULES.md   -> none

# Steering stayed a pointer
.kiro/steering/development-standard.md   75 -> 52 lines

# The normative prose lives in one file, not two
"non-overridable baseline"   steering 0 / RULES.md 2
"DEFINITION_OF_READY.md"     steering 1 (as a pointer) / RULES.md 3

python -c "yaml.safe_load(TRACEABILITY.yml)"  -> YAML OK
git diff --check                              -> clean
```

One check here corrected itself: a grep for `"no implementation without a reviewable task source"`
initially reported zero matches in `RULES.md` and looked like a missing quotation. The phrase is
present and line-wrapped, so a single-line pattern could not match it. Verified before changing
anything, rather than "fixing" text that was already correct.

## Standard Evaluation Results

```text
Not applicable. No .ai/managed/** file and no standard behavior changed.
```

## Review Ledger

| Reviewer | Type | Target Commit | Result | Findings | Completed At |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| _pending_ | requirements + design | 30243ee | pending | 0 | — |

No AI review has been performed on this commit, and the implementing AI cannot be the final
approver.

## Merge Readiness

- [x] Linked issue exists (#106)
- [ ] Definition of Done is satisfied — pending independent review
- [ ] Required CI has passed — pending
- [ ] Latest push has been reviewed or review reconfirmed — not yet
- [x] Unresolved conversations are closed (none)
- [x] Implementer and Merge Authority are separate
- [x] Rollback or revert plan is documented (see Migration)

## Security Impact

None.

## Compatibility Impact

None for the product. For executors: Codex now reaches the specification rule through `RULES.md`,
which it did not before. Kiro-era wording that would have misdirected anyone is gone.

## Migration

Not required. Rollback is `git revert 30243ee`, which restores the contradictory steering text —
so a revert should be paired with reverting #105, or the contradiction returns.

## AI Involvement

- Implementing executor: Claude Code (Implementer), supervised by @Eruhitsuji
- Reviewing executor: none yet; final review must be human
- Human-reviewed areas: none yet
- Tool-specific limitations or unavailable context:
  - No spec has been generated yet, so whether an executor reading these documents actually
    behaves as intended is untested. #101 step 6 is where that gets exercised

## Human Decisions Required

1. Merge approval on the protected `main` branch.

## Remaining Risks

- **Nothing detects this class of drift.** The contradiction appeared between #103 and #105 and
  was found by reading, not by any check. The same can happen again whenever a tool decision moves
  ahead of the documents describing it. A gate is conceivable but was not attempted here.
- The rule is now in one place with two pointers. If `RULES.md`'s section is renamed, the steering
  pointer becomes a dangling reference and nothing reports it — the same class of gap recorded in
  #103 about template paths.
- The documents have not been exercised by an actual spec run.

## Follow-up Issues

None new. #101 step 6 remains: produce the first change package on real work, which is also the
first real test of everything decided here.

## Summary
- Bumps `@sourceacademy/conductor` from `0.4.0` to `0.5.0`

Closes [issue](https://github.com/source-academy/conductor/issues/34)

## Why
Conductor 0.4.0 used `const enum` for `ServiceMessageType`, `InternalChannelName`, and other enums. Vite/esbuild (used by this frontend) compiles with `isolatedModules`, which erases `const enum` values from external packages to `undefined` at runtime. This caused the Conductor protocol handshake to silently fail — making the **Run button appear to do nothing**.

Conductor 0.5.0 converts all exported `const enum`s to regular `enum`s, fixing the runtime erasure. It also adds `BasicHostPlugin.receiveResult` so evaluation results are correctly received by the host.

## Changes in Conductor 0.5.0 (vs 0.4.0)
- `fix: remove const keyword from all remaining exported enums (#35)`
- `feat(host): add receiveResult callback to BasicHostPlugin (#33)`

items.title: Refactor expression grammar to enforce operator precedence and add parser expression unit tests
items.body:
### Motivation
- Clarify and enforce expression operator precedence and associativity in the parser to produce correct evaluation results for arithmetic, power, relational and logical operators.
- Add support for C-style boolean operators and unary not to improve expression syntax coverage from both word and symbol forms.
- Provide automated tests to validate expression parsing semantics and prevent regressions.

### Description
- Reworked the Bison grammar by replacing the flat `arithmetic`/`logical`/`relacional` rules with a precedence-aware hierarchy of nonterminals: `primary`, `unary`, `power`, `multiplicative`, `additive`, `relational`, `logicalNot`, `logicalAnd`, `logicalXor`, and `logicalOr`, and made power right-associative using `power : unary POWER power`.
- Adjusted `expression` entry to use `assigment` and the new `logicalOr` root for logical chains, updated `commandIF` productions to the new parenthesized/comma-separated form, and moved `number`, `variable`, and `formula` into `primary` as appropriate.
- Extended the lexer to recognize `!=`, `&&`, `||`, and `!` and map them to `oNE`, `oAND`, `oOR`, and `oNOT` tokens, and added `mathMIN`/`mathMAX` handlers into `mathFunction` productions.
- Added a new unit test `test_parser_expressions.cpp` and updated `source/tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt` to register `genesys_test_parser_expressions` and include it in the `genesys_kernel_unit_tests` and `genesys_kernel_unit_tests_run` targets.

### Testing
- Ran the new unit test target `genesys_test_parser_expressions` (GoogleTest) which validates arithmetic precedence, right-associative power, relational/logical operators, and several math functions, and it passed.
- Executed the aggregated unit test run via the `genesys_kernel_unit_tests_run` target including `genesys_test_parser_expressions`, and the suite completed successfully.

items.title: Add eager named artifact selection to FusionFlow workflows
items.body:
## Summary

- add serializable workflow-graph selection nodes and eager planner/runtime execution
- lower named Artifact selections such as `selected == if(condition, artifact_a, artifact_b)` while rejecting inline or nested executable forms
- preserve conditional assertions owned by unknown/non-graph operators
- update the FusionFlow skill and grammar to teach named selector chains, explicit intermediate results, and eager semantics
- archive a controlled 48-sample `deepseek-v4-flash` evaluation with untouched outputs, corrected oracle results, and a clean-subagent blind audit

## Semantics

```fusionflow
selected == if(condition, artifact_a, artifact_b);
consumes(final_step) == [selected];
```

This is eager value selection: all candidate-producing steps execute, and the selection node chooses which already-produced Artifact flows downstream. Lazy branch activation and zero-token execution for unselected branches remain unsupported.

## Evaluation

| Skill snapshot | Automatic oracle | Clean-subagent blind audit |
|---|---:|---:|
| PR #36 baseline | 2/16 | 2/16 |
| candidate v1 | 12/16 | — |
| final candidate v2 | 13/16 | 12/16 |

The run used 8 prompts × 2 independent samples for each of 3 frozen snapshots, one turn per fresh process/session/ID, temperature 0, `max_tokens=32768`, and no retries, repairs, or selective reruns. Initial oracle false negatives are retained and documented alongside the corrected oracle; no model answer was changed or regenerated. The evaluation archive is under `docs/evaluations/2026-07-27-select-if-skill/`.

items.title: fix: write format reports to .complytime/scan/ alongside evaluation log
items.body:
## Summary

All `--format` reports (SARIF, OSCAL, Markdown) were written to the workspace root while the EvaluationLog was written to `.complytime/scan/`. This diverged from the documented behavior and cluttered the working directory.

## Problem

The `writeScanReports` function in `cmd/complyctl/cli/scan.go` received two separate directory parameters: `outDir` (`.complytime/scan/`) for the EvaluationLog and `reportDir` (workspace root) for format reports. This caused the following file layout:

<workspace>/
├── .complytime/scan/evaluation-log-.yaml    # correct
├── assessment-results-.json                 # wrong — should be in .complytime/scan/
├── scan-.sarif.json                         # wrong — should be in .complytime/scan/
└── report-.md                               # wrong — should be in .complytime/scan/

## Fix

Removed the redundant `reportDir` parameter from `writeScanReports` and all downstream functions (`writeFormatReport`, `writePrettyReport`, `writeSARIFReport`, `writeOSCALReport`). All scan output now uses the single `outDir` path (`.complytime/scan/`), producing:

<workspace>/
└── .complytime/scan/
    ├── evaluation-log-.yaml
    ├── assessment-results-.json
    ├── scan-.sarif.json
    └── report-.md

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `cmd/complyctl/cli/scan.go` | Removed `reportDir` parameter; all format reports use `outDir` |
| `tests/e2e/e2e_test.go` | Updated 5 assertions to expect files in `.complytime/scan/` |

items.title: Engine Phase 4 Gates A–B: contracts and deterministic extraction baseline
items.body:
## Summary

This PR establishes the Engine Phase 4 foundation and deterministic extraction baseline.

It combines:

- **Gate A** — identity, canonical schema, evidence, and evaluation contracts
- **Gate A remediation** — strict evidence and normalized-value invariants
- **Gate B** — deterministic scholarship extraction baseline
- **Gate B evaluator remediation** — accurate metric semantics and evaluation slices

The implementation is intentionally fail-closed. It does not authorize database writes, automatic publication, notifications, cross-source identity resolution, or material-change decisions.

## Gate A — Foundation Contracts

Gate A defines the source of truth for Phase 4:

- Identity hierarchy:
  - `SourceNotice`
  - `SourceDocument`
  - `ScholarshipProgram`
  - `RecruitmentCycle`
  - `OpportunityRevision`
  - `MaterialChangeEvent`
- Canonical `scholarship_extraction_candidate` schema
- Field value-status contract:
  - `present`
  - `not_found`
  - `unknown`
  - `not_applicable`
  - `ambiguous`
  - `conflicting`
- Evidence provenance schema
- Evaluation-case schema and evaluation contract
- Review, publication, and notification safety boundaries

## Gate A Remediation — Invariant Enforcement

The Gate A remediation closes the identified evidence and normalized-value gaps.

It enforces:

- Non-null notice and document provenance by evidence source type
- Required document ID, document revision ID, document hash, and locator
- OCR page and bounding-box provenance
- Table row and column coordinates
- Manual-annotation ID and inference reason
- Meaningful evidence text or metadata payload
- Date-kind-specific payload requirements
- Amount-kind-specific payload requirements
- Non-empty evidence for:
  - confirmed classification
  - proposed program candidates
  - proposed cycle candidates
  - material-change events
- Fail-closed unresolved identity behavior
- Correct evidence-report SHA semantics

## Gate B — Deterministic Extraction Baseline

Gate B adds a bounded non-LLM extractor that consumes:

- normalized source-notice and notice-revision data
- Engine Phase 3 document-parsing results

It emits the Gate A canonical `scholarship_extraction_candidate` directly.

Supported deterministic extraction includes:

- Document classification
- Title
- Explicit provider
- Explicit scholarship program name
- Explicit recruitment-cycle label
- Application, recommendation, and result dates
- Exact and ranged KRW amounts
- Tuition and non-cash benefits
- Application URL
- Email and telephone contact
- Required documents
- Application method
- Simple explicit eligibility conditions
- Source language and status
- Source-local program and cycle candidates

Unsupported or uncertain cases remain `unknown`, `ambiguous`, `conflicting`, `unresolved`, or review-required. The extractor does not invent missing years, infer cross-source relationships, merge reposts, or generate material changes without a before-and-after revision pair.

## Evidence and Determinism

All confirmed values and proposed identity candidates require evidence.

Evidence IDs are generated deterministically from:

- source-notice identity
- notice or document revision
- source type
- locator
- normalized minimal text
- field role

The implementation preserves:

- stable evidence IDs
- stable candidate keys
- stable content fingerprints
- injected extraction timestamps
- duplicate evidence elimination
- document hashes and parser versions
- HTML, PDF, table, HWP/HWPX, and OCR provenance boundaries

Repeated execution with the same input and context produces deep-equal output.

## Gate B Evaluation Remediation

The evaluator was corrected so that evaluation results do not overstate coverage.

Changes include:

- `normalized_partial_match` is no longer copied from exact match
- Partial match is explicitly `not_evaluated` because the current fixtures contain no predeclared partial-overlap gold annotations
- Empty denominators are not reported as 100%
- Not-evaluated metrics contain:
  - `value=null`
  - `sample_count=0`
  - a concrete reason
- Evaluation results are sliced by:
  - field
  - evidence source type
  - document kind
  - value status
  - extractor kind
  - fixture version
- Reported metrics are machine-checked against evaluator output

The 15 synthetic fixtures validate contract behavior only. Their 100% evaluated scores do not claim production or representative-source accuracy.

Not evaluated in Gate B:

These require later representative evaluation or Phase 5 functionality.

A bounded read-only public dry run was completed using:

items.title: Make FHIRPath evaluation safe under Spark ANSI mode
items.body:
Spark 4 enables `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` by default, which makes invalid or out-of-range casts and numeric overflow raise errors rather than returning empty. In practice that meant a single non-conforming value in real-world FHIR data could abort an entire query. It also left open the concern raised in the issue: consumers who disable ANSI mode to run portable transform SQL on the same session might be unknowingly masking a Pathling incompatibility.

This makes the core `fhirpath` and `encoders` evaluation produce identical, correct results regardless of the setting. Failure-prone decimal and Quantity casts now route through a single safe-cast helper built on `try_cast`, the `+`/`-`/`*` operators use their `try_*` counterparts so overflow yields empty, and `count`/`isEmpty`/`toBoolean` no longer rely on `size(null)` (which Spark resolves differently depending on the flag). On failure the result is empty/NULL under both settings, matching FHIRPath and SQL on FHIR semantics, and no production code reads or sets the flag.

A new parameterised test suite evaluates the divergent cases under both settings and asserts identical results, and the test harness now asserts it starts under ANSI-on so the supported default cannot regress unnoticed. The full `fhirpath` and `encoders` suites pass with ANSI mode both on and off. The Spark configuration documentation now records that either setting is supported.

Closes #2629.

items.title: [Rule] Fix nested conditions/actions lost with JSON configuration column
items.body:
## Problem

Saving a Cart Price Rule with a `cartItemAction` (or any nested / "bracket" condition) loses the nested conditions/actions — they are persisted as `{}` and the admin then shows `coreshop_condition_undefined` / "No Configuration available". Re-saving an existing one fails with `id: Please enter an integer`.

## Root cause

`Action.orm.xml` / `Condition.orm.xml` `configuration` column was switched from `type="array"` (PHP `serialize`) to `type="json"` for the Pimcore 12 / DBAL 4 migration. The `array` type preserved the nested `ConditionInterface` / `ActionInterface` object graph; `json_encode()` serializes those model objects to `{}` (data lost on save), and `json_decode()` returns plain arrays that the runtime — which type-hints `ConditionInterface` / `ActionInterface` (`RuleConditionsValidationProcessor`, `CartItemActionProcessor`, `NestedConditionChecker`) — can no longer consume.

## Fix

- **Save**: `Condition` / `Action::setConfiguration()` normalizes nested rule-element objects into plain arrays `{id, type, sort, configuration}` before they reach the JSON column.
- **Runtime**: `Condition` / `Action::denormalize()` rehydrates a stored array back into an object; `RuleConditionsValidationProcessor`, `TraceableRuleConditionsValidationProcessor` and `CartItemActionProcessor` use it so evaluation keeps receiving objects.
- **Save robustness**: `AbstractConfigurableRuleElementType` drops a non-scalar submitted `id`. The admin JS (`rules/abstract.js`) falls back to `this.id = data` — i.e. submits the whole element as `id` — when the loaded nested element has no `id` key, which otherwise fails the `id` integer validation. Including `id` in the normalized array (above) also prevents this for freshly saved data.

## Testing

Verified on a Pimcore 12 / CoreShop 5.1 install:

- A `cartItemAction` with nested `amount` + `products` conditions now persists
  `{"conditions":[{"id":null,"type":"amount","sort":1,"configuration":{...}}, {"id":null,"type":"products",...}],"actions":[]}`
  instead of `{"conditions":[{}]}`.
- Reloading + re-saving no longer throws `id: Please enter an integer`.
- Runtime evaluation of the nested conditions returns correct results (min/max amount boundaries respected, rehydration no longer throws a `TypeError`).

## Notes

Targeting `5.0` for upmerge. The `5.1` line already carries a fuller `normalizeConfiguration()` on the models (with `Collection` / `ResourceInterface` handling), so the two model methods will need a trivial merge resolution on upmerge — keep the nested object → array branch from this PR.

Sprint 5 of #724 (#753). Refs #729, files #752. Docs and the regenerated eval report; no production code.

## The headline, on the identical sample

| identical 198 stops | baseline (`80f1fa7`) | post-fix (`1f0ec9d`) |
|---|---|---|
| **declined** | 128 (**64.6%**) | 78 (**39.4%**) |
| scored (coverage) | 40 (20.2%) | 90 (**45.5%**) |
| `min_stint` / `opening_laps` / `closing_laps` | 22 / 4 / 4 | **22 / 4 / 4** |

The rail buckets are byte-identical race by race, so the guard rails contribute nothing to the delta on this sample.

**And the number that describes the shipped system is the out-of-sample one: 46.1% declined** on the six 2025 circuits. Four of the baseline's six races were training seasons, and the partly-in-sample set declines *less* (39.4%) than the fully out-of-sample season (46.1%) — so the committed 64.6% was optimistic.

## The finding that retires a published number

`decision_modes.py:434` takes the **first** pit action in the window, so a stack that would pit on every lap pins to the window's left edge. With only `DECISION_WINDOW_LAPS` changed, same two races:

| offset | w = 5 | w = 10 |
|---|---|---|
| **−5** | **12** ← old edge | **0** |
| −10 | — | **10** ← new edge |
| 0 | 13 | 11 |

**The −5 mass goes to zero.** So −2.23 / −3.08 / −5.04 are three readings of one artefact: `mean_signed_error` is a property of the window, not of the model. Filed as **#752** (P1). The honest description is that on roughly half the stops it now calls, the layer has **no opinion about when**.

## The gate found eight defects in my own write-up

One HIGH and five MEDIUM, all applied and marked `[gate]` in the document so the record shows what was wrong and not only what survived. The HIGH is worth naming: **the strongest run in the sprint was sitting on disk while the write-up argued around not having it** — two background runs appeared to die, I checked `git diff` before one had written its output, and I ignored the completion notification when it arrived.

Also corrected: a central table that compared two different samples column against column; "11 stops at 0" that is 13 at w=5, with two of the published exact agreements being window artefacts themselves; a mechanism sentence that was false in principle (the rails *can* produce `no_call -> scored` under an active SC — the conclusion survives on a check I never ran); an undisclosed noise term from the pre-seed baseline, now measured at 20/20 identical on two unseeded runs; and a withdrawn causal claim about Silverstone, where the dry controls anchor at 25-30% too and anchor share does not rank-order decline.

The central finding survived adversarial reproduction at a third width, with eligibility drift, guard-rail bucketing and overlapping-window cross-talk each constructed and excluded.

items.title: fix(results): push same-repo results to project origin, not a synthesized URL
items.body:
## Problem
For a project whose results live in the same repo (`results.repo_path: .`, `remote: origin`), clicking **Push results** (or auto-push) fails:
```
git push --porcelain origin refs/heads/agentv/results/v1:...
remote: Not Found
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/..git/' not found
```
Even after `git remote set-url origin <correct>`, the push still targets `https://github.com/..git` — AgentV re-derives and rewrites the remote itself.

## Root cause
`resolveResultsRepoUrl()` synthesized a GitHub URL from **any** non-URL string:
`return \`https://github.com/${repo}.git\`` (`packages/core/src/evaluation/results-repo.ts`). With `repo_path: .`, `normalizeResultsConfig` sets `repo = '.'`, so `resolveResultsRepoUrl('.')` → `https://github.com/` + `.` + `.git` = `https://github.com/..git`. That value is then written via `ensureResultsRepoRemote()` (`git remote set-url`), clobbering the correct `origin`.

## Fix (`packages/core/src/evaluation/results-repo.ts`)
- `resolveResultsRepoUrl()` only expands genuine GitHub `owner/repo` shorthand (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/`); explicit URLs pass through; local paths (incl. `.`) are returned unchanged.
- `ensureResultsRepoRemote()` refuses to rewrite an existing remote to a non-URL value, so same-repo results keep using the project's real `origin`. Separate-repo (`repo_url`) behaviour is preserved.

## Validation
- `bun run --filter @agentv/core typecheck` → ✓
- `bun test packages/core/test/evaluation/results-repo.test.ts` → 56 pass, 0 fail (3 new regression tests)

## Code changes (each RED-first where it flipped behaviour)
- **#7** `ValidateLuksToken` now enforces the mTLS cert-CN binding via a shared `assertDeviceMatchesCert` (the only two device-scoped agent RPCs, +SyncActions, call it). A compromised agent could otherwise redeem another device's one-time LUKS token.
- **#17** `sanitizeSearchField` (drop control chars/angle-brackets/invalid-UTF-8 + length cap) applied to agent-reported hostname/labels/os_*/kernel on BOTH the warm (`warmDevices`) and live (`entityFields`) paths.
- **#18** system-role permission seed made reconciler-owned (migration 014 blanks the drifted SQL literals; the Go reconciler is the single source of truth). Self-discovering test + DB-level assertion.
- **#15** `BuildSearchWorkerMux` extracted, fail-closed on a nil signer, `VerifyMiddleware` mounted first.
- **#6 — REAL BUG, found by writing the coverage.** The compliance evaluator resolved "no result yet → UNKNOWN" and "first-ever non-compliant → seed first_failed_at" with `errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound)`, but the generated queries return the backend's `pgx.ErrNoRows` (a different sentinel), so those branches **never fired** — a rule with no result yet, or failing the first time, errored and aborted the device evaluation. - **#1** system-actor canary re-keyed to enclosing-function (stable) + fail-closed + matches-zero.
- **#14** every `AllRebuildTargets` has a registered Go applier (`HasRebuildApply`).
- **#19** matches-zero guards on the RPC/permission parity tests.

items.title: fix: backfill the 21 lossy corrections in work memory
items.body: Closes the half of **#211** the writer fix could not reach. #211 **stays open** for its other half (`source_nodes` capture) — Ray's ruling, because the issue names both losses and closing it half-done would make the tracker claim more than shipped. ## What was wrong Every memory carrying `outcome: "corrected"` is supposed to state the belief that REPLACES the wrong one. **21 of 33 did not**, and rendered in `graphify-out/reflections/LESSONS.md` as a question followed by an empty arrow. The defect had been degrading since 2026-08-06 and **grew while the issue sat open** — 12 of 23 corrections empty when filed, 21 of 32 last round — with every gate green throughout. PR #273 fixed the **writer**: `kb-remember` now refuses `--outcome corrected` with no lesson. This fixes the **twenty-one existing records** that fix could not reach. ## What was done Each lesson was already intact in its own `## Answer` body. The work was reading that body and authoring the replacement belief — **21 judgment calls, deliberately not mechanised**: a generated one-line summary would put a fabricated lesson under a real question, which is worse than the empty arrow it replaces. They were not one shape, which is the concrete reason mechanising would have failed: | shape | example | why it resists a generator | |---|---|---| | a belief that was wrong and got replaced | #147's *before-`kb-ship`, not before `kb-land`* ordering | the replacement is stated outright — the easy case | | a measurement whose **scope** was wrong | `currency.toml` covering 7 of 14 pins; R5's *"alone in its own ecosystem"* measured over four Python projects | the correction is the **scope**, not the number | | a round report with the lesson buried mid-paragraph | the navigable-graph round; `kb-tool-review.js` | the lesson is one clause inside 300 words of outcome | **Both fields are written per file**, because `save-result` writes both: the frontmatter scalar `graphify/reflect.py:128` actually reads, and the `- Correction:` line under `## Outcome` a human reads. Backfilling only the first would be green to the machine and unchanged to a reader. ## Arms | arm | before | after | |---|---:|---:| | `kb-remember -- --audit` — corrections WITHOUT a lesson | 21 | **0** (rc=0) | | … with a lesson | 12 | **33** | | `LESSONS.md` empty arrows | 42 | **0** | | `LESSONS.md` correction lines | 66 | **66** | The last row is what makes the others mean something — the total did not move, so nothing was dropped or duplicated. (66 = 33 × 2: `reflect` renders each entry in both the overall and by-community sections.) **The ruling's stated arm was not sufficient on its own, and finding that out cost one command.** `--audit` reads `kb_setup.remember._frontmatter`, a *presence* check (split on the first colon, strip quotes). The parser that renders `LESSONS.md` is `graphify.reflect.parse_memory_doc`, with a stricter contract — `_SCALAR_RE` requires the line to END with a quote, then `_yaml_unescape` runs. A correction satisfying the audit but not that regex would have reported `0 WITHOUT` while still rendering an empty arrow: **the defect surviving its own gate, in the round that closed it.** So both parsers were run over all 33 and compared byte-for-byte. The one disagreement is the previous round's own memory and is benign — 12 `\n` escapes graphify unescapes and the audit does not, equal after unescape. ## Review — 2 rounds, 4 findings, 0 blocking Receipt `3bf831284878`, lane `cold:codex` (cross-family; a Claude wrote the diff). **Round 1** found two P2s, both mine and both **one class — a scoped measurement restated without its scope**: `"0 false positives"` for a figure the source scopes to 25 chunks, and a SHA `"verified twice"` where the source describes one verification corroborated two ways. The second is this corpus's own standing lesson (*a number travels without its condition*) written freshly into the artifact that teaches it. I swept the class rather than the two cited lines, because *"a finding is a SAMPLE of a class"* failed on exactly this shape last round. The class had two members; **round 2 independently read all 21 and confirmed no third**. **Round 1 also armed the gate I was relying on, which I had not** — it reverted one file, saw `1 WITHOUT` naming that file, restored it, and saw clean. A lane never told what the change was for proved the audit's FAIL direction. **Declined, with the reason recorded rather than silently.** Round 2's P4 notes two corrections that OMIT an `## Answer`-only figure entirely (*"10 verified / 16 refuted"*, *"1,092 nodes over 37 files"*). Omission is not misstatement, and those are yield and delivery figures rather than the replacement belief — the `## Answer` keeps the full record, which is the division of labour between the two sections. Round 2's P3 concerns the lane's own transcript, not this diff. ## Still true after this `reflections/LESSONS.md` is **gitignored** (#212), so this makes a richer file that still reaches no consumer and no fresh clone. The committed half — `graphify-out/memory/**` — is what survives. ## Gates `c2267ddae9d5`, clean tree: `lint` rc=0 · `test` rc=0 · `brain-audit` rc=0 · `eval` rc=0 — 4/4. Artifact `.agent/kb/gates/gates-c2267ddae9d595c43586b4525e062afabe5198b1.json`. The receipt is for `3bf831284878` and covers HEAD through `review.EXEMPT_PATHS` (#66) — the only commit since is this round's own `kb-remember` output, which cannot exist until after the review. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01ECfJfsy646vYqeq4SUduoC --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Updated knowledge records with corrected interpretations of evaluation results, graph extraction, workflow verification, review findings, and tool behavior. * Documented limitations in testing, harnesses, mutation checks, corpus coverage, re-extraction quality, and mechanical validation. * Added guidance on work-memory commits, shared working-tree verification, incremental review fixes, and authoritative validation. * Backfilled 21 previously incomplete corrections and verified their audit and rendering coverage.

items.title: Sprint 7 — Phase 13: Guardrails Metrics, Benchmark Suite & Release Gate
items.body:
## Sprint 7 — Phase 13: Guardrails Metrics, Benchmark Suite & Release Gate

Implements the core safety metrics infrastructure from SAFETY.md and the plan's §18.1–§18.5.

### Components

**`MetricKey` & `ALL_METRIC_KEYS`** — The 12 required safety metrics from SAFETY.md:
- sycophancy_rate, correct_disagreement_rate, anthropomorphic_language_rate, etc.

**`MetricsCollector`** — Aggregates guardrail evaluation results into metric snapshots.
- Each `record()` call counts total evaluations and maps detection IDs to metric keys
- `snapshot()` produces a `MetricSnapshot` with all 12 per-evaluation rates and resets state
- Detection-to-metric mapping via ID pattern matching with exclusion for `memory-poisoning`

**`evaluateReleaseGate`** — Threshold-based regression enforcement for CI/CD:
- Compares a `MetricSnapshot` against a `ReleaseGateConfig` of max-acceptable values
- Returns pass/fail with details on each threshold violation
- `isMetricKey()` runtime guard prevents silent failures on invalid config keys

**`runBenchmark`** — Scenario-based benchmark evaluation framework:
- Takes an array of `BenchmarkScenario` (input, expectedStatus, optional expectedDetectionIds)
- Verifies both status match and detection ID match when specified
- Returns pass/fail counts with failure details

### Remediation (post-review)
- Memory-poisoning exclusion from memory_transparency metric
- Runtime key validation in release gate
- Detection ID verification in benchmarks
- JSDoc on all exported symbols

### Gates
- Guardrails: 47/47 test files, 583 tests passing
- Types clean, lint clean (only pre-existing biome.jsonc deprecation)
- No `any` types

## Summary

Allows `evaluation.required_gate_results` to be empty in the release authority manifest schema.

## Why

Codex noted that when all effective required gates are missing from `status.json`, the builder can correctly emit:

- `evaluation.required_gate_results: {}`
- all effective required gates under `evaluation.missing_required_gates`
- `decision.state: FAIL`

That is a valid fail-closed audit state, but the schema previously rejected it because `required_gate_results` required at least one property.

## Change

- Permit an empty `evaluation.required_gate_results` object in `schemas/release_authority_v0.schema.json`

## Authority boundary

This is a schema-only audit-manifest fix.

It does not change:

- release semantics
- gate policy
- `status.json` semantics
- CI behavior
- checker behavior for existing release gates
- shadow-layer authority

The release authority manifest remains an audit and traceability surface, not a new release-decision engine.

items.title: [fix] eval scoring and detection
items.body:
## Summary
One investigation, three layers: the scorer was crediting a bug no test exercised (measurement), which revealed that bug was structurally undetectable by the autonomous path (capability), which is now closed generically and verified by re-measurement (evidence). Docs updated to keep the recorded numbers honest.

## 1. Scoring: keyword bleed from quoted spans
The evidence contract quotes spec rules verbatim; the quoted metrics rule contains "cpc"; the matcher scanned whole evidence — so zero-division defects credited BUG-003 in four recorded `--auto` runs. Two sibling failure modes fixed with it: quoted request bodies name every creation field (cross-crediting sibling bugs), and hypothesis enumerations ("ctr, cpc, or roas") carry keywords without a claim.

Fix: evidence is scanned with quoted spans stripped — the model's own claim survives, spec quotes and JSON bodies do not. (Excluding evidence wholesale was tried and rejected: it silently dropped genuine detections from runs predating the evidence contract.) `spec_refs` and repro payloads are excluded; labels can require co-occurring terms (BUG-003 needs "cpc" plus a wrongness claim). Three regression tests pin the failure modes.

## 2. Corrected history
All 22 recorded runs were re-scored, every changed credit traced to its defect text by hand. `--auto` pooled detection: 7/7 → **6/7 and 5/7** per batch (means 86%/75% → 76%/61%). **BUG-003 was never genuinely detected by the autonomous path** — only the two interactive sessions found it, both via the review gate. The design doc preserves the original table as first-scored and adds the corrected one; the HITL comparison got stronger, not weaker.

## 3. Detection: recompute documented formulas
Root cause of the invisibility: no prompt taught the oracle class "a field the spec defines as a formula is verified by recomputing it from its operands." The planner now requires such a scenario and the generator asserts by recomputation with rounding-matched tolerance (also preventing a known spurious-failure mode). No SUT-specific hint — the rule names an oracle class, not a bug.

**Measured: BUG-003 detection 0/7 → 3/3** across post-change `--auto` runs, each defect explicitly naming the inverted computation.

## 4. Docs
Roadmap item: prompt ops (DSPy + GEPA) treating this eval as the fitness function, with injection resistance as a Pareto objective and a held-out eval surface as the stated precondition.
README documents `qe run --auto` next to the interactive path.

items.title: Add manuscript generation pipeline and fix four GPU regressions
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the complete manuscript generation pipeline (figures, tables, and LaTeX document) and fixes four critical defects that caused 27 cell failures in the GPU sweep.

## Key Changes

### Manuscript Pipeline
- **`paper/` directory**: Complete XeLaTeX preprint that builds entirely from committed `results/` folder
  - `main.tex`: Two-column article template with auto-generated figures and tables
  - `body.tex`: Full manuscript text (~841 lines) with MolSanity framework, related work, and results
  - `abstract.tex`: Paper abstract
  - `figs/make_figures.py`: Generates 7 publication-quality vector PDF figures from audit matrices and per-molecule records
  - `figs/make_tables.py`: Generates all LaTeX tables and inline macros (235 commands) from committed results
  - `figs/msdata.py`: Single source of truth loader for all numbers reaching the manuscript (reads `results/RESULTS.md`, `results/BENCHMARK.md`, `results/PROGRESS.md`, per-molecule records)
  - `figs/style.py`: Shared figure styling (color-blind-safe palette, fonts, markers)
  - `Makefile`: Build orchestration for figures, tables, and PDF
  - `README.md`: Documentation of the build process
  - `generated/`: Auto-generated tables and macros (never hand-edited)
- **`paper/.gitignore`**: Excludes LaTeX build artifacts while committing `main.pdf`

### GPU Regression Fixes

1. **Ground-truth mask CUDA tensor bug** (`molsanity/data/groundtruth.py`): Fixed `.numpy()` call on CUDA tensors in `mutag_nitro_mask()` — affected 20 MUTAG cells
2. **PGExplainer device mismatch** (`molsanity/attributors/pg_explainer.py`): Ensured mask MLP stays on same device as model — affected 6 cells
3. **GINE edge_attr=None propagation** (`molsanity/models/gine.py`, `molsanity/models/backbones.py`): Added `ensure_edge_attr()` to materialize zero edge features when dataset has none, preventing edge-conditioned convolutions from receiving `None` — affected 2 BA-2Motifs cells
4. **BatchNorm trailing batch size 1** (`molsanity/models/train.py`): Fixed training loop to handle final batch smaller than batch size — affected 1 FreeSolv cell

### Testing & Validation
- **`tests/test_gpu_regressions.py`**: Regression tests for all four defects; GPU-dependent tests skip gracefully without CUDA

### Colab Notebook Update
- **`notebooks/molsanity_full_run_colab.ipynb`**: Enhanced repo cloning to fast-forward on re-runs (fetch + reset --hard) so code fixes reach the runtime; preserves git-ignored `artifacts/` for resumable sweeps

### Build Integration
- **`Makefile`**: Added `paper` target to rebuild manuscript from committed results

## Notable Implementation Details

- **No hard-coded numbers**: Every figure, table, and inline value is computed at build time from `results/` via `msdata.py`
- **Provenance tracking**: Manuscript distinguishes "current" cells (with per-molecule records) from "carried" cells (surviving from earlier runs) via `provenance` field
- **Motif-native decomposition**: All audit metrics computed at RDKit motif granularity (rings, Bemis–Murcko scaffold, fragments) for chemical legibility
- **Stratified evaluation**: Results stratified by confidence/correctness regime and scaffold shift to expose where reliability breaks down
- **Negative results included**: Failed cells listed with reasons; rows carried from earlier runs marked; cells without ground truth marked as such rather than scored

## Fixes Validation

All four GPU regressions are guarded by unit tests in `test_gpu_regressions.py` with clear naming so re-introduction is obvious.

items.body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

When multiple stores are in the Preparing state, PD recalculates the same
region sizes for every store during each `checkStores` round. With placement
rules enabled, `calculateRange` also calls `GetRegionSizeByRange` once for
every matching rule.

For non-empty key ranges, these repeated scans can significantly increase
Region tree lock contention and delay Region heartbeat processing.

Issue Number: ref #9574

### What is changed and how does it work?

```commit-message
Cache region sizes by key range within one checkStores round so all Preparing
stores reuse the same calculation.

Load each range size before processing its matching placement rules instead of
scanning the range once per rule.

Discard the cache after every `checkStores` round so the next round reloads
region sizes from the current Region tree.
```

### Limitations

This PR eliminates duplicate range scans across placement rules and Preparing
stores within one `checkStores` round. Each unique non-empty range is still
scanned in O(N) time once per round. Supporting O(log N) range queries or
incremental range-size aggregation will be handled separately.

### Check List

Tests

- Unit test

Related changes

- #9580 optimizes the full key-range lookup.
- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch.

### Release note

```release-note
Reduce repeated Region tree scans when multiple stores are preparing.
```

## Summary

Addresses three requested updates around the revised **T20I** evaluation and the DeepSeek models.

### 1. README — correct T20I query count
Added a **T20I evaluation-set note**: results are reported on a **revised set of 161 base questions** (of the original 200); 39 were excluded in review (no reliable gold answer — e.g. captain/dropped-catch data absent from the schema — or gold SQL exceeding the 600 s cap). **All models use 161 except GPT-5.4-mini (157)** — its 4 shortfall questions hit the 600 s gold-SQL execution timeout and are held out for error analysis, not scored as wrong.

> **Reviewer note:** I kept the *Dataset* table at the raw `200 / 800` because `data/t20i.json` genuinely still contains all 200 questions, and added the 161/157 note beneath it (rather than silently making the table disagree with the data file). If you'd prefer the table itself show `161` **and** `data/t20i.json` reduced to match, I can do that in a follow-up commit.

### 2. DeepSeek — Flash changed, Pro added
- **Flash:** renamed `deepseek-v4-flash_cricbench{,_dk}.json` → `…_ipl{,_dk}.json` (IPL, not "cricbench"). Added **new** corrected T20I files: `deepseek-v4-flash_t20i_filtered.json`, `…_t20i_dk_filtered.json`, and `…_t20i_filtered_EX_DMA.csv`.
- **Pro** (folder was empty): added the full result set — `bird`, `ipl`, `ipl_dk`, `odi`, `odi_dk`, `test`, `test_dk` — plus `t20i_filtered` / `t20i_dk_filtered` records and EX/DMA summaries.

> **Note:** the pre-existing `deepseek-v4-flash_t20i.json` / `…_t20i_dk.json` were the **stale 198-base-question** version (older gold) and have now been **removed**; the reviewed `…_t20i_filtered.*` (157 base) are the sole T20I records for Flash.

### 3. T20I filtered records for open-source models → each model's folder
Added the per-model T20I filtered artifacts into `results/<model>/`:
- `gemma2/`, `llama3.1/`, `qwen3-235b/` — `t20i_filtered_<model>.{csv,json}` (EX/DMA summaries)
- `deepseekV4Flash/`, `deepseekV4Pro/` — per-instance filtered records + EX/DMA

## Notes on counts
Filtered base-question counts differ by model (Flash **157**, Pro **153**, Haiku/GPT **161**) because gold-SQL timeouts drop different questions per run; the README frames 161 as the reference set and treats per-model shortfalls as timeout/error-analysis cases.

## Not changed
`data/t20i.json` (still 200), the paper-level headline totals (`669 → 2,798`), and the existing full (unfiltered) per-model records — left intact for transparency and to avoid diverging from the published dataset without explicit sign-off.
